policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV JDG.6.5 has no note at this word, and its 'they came up' does not distinguish the qere (waw-consecutive perfect) from the ketiv imperfect: in this iterative account of the Midianite raids an imperfect is rendered by the same English past ('they came in as locusts', 'they came into the land' in the same verse), so the English wording is compatible with both readings. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
